Not would I think anyone lie about that, having said concerning the holy prophets, that not only they received of the coming things the knowledge, the shining of the matter to them of the Holy Spirit, and sounding into the mind, but also indeed of them it is, when of the things having said that they became beholders. It seems therefore the blessed prophet Isaiah to the eyes of the intellect the sufferings about to come concerning Judah to have been seen, this indeed the phalanxes of the enemies trampling the earth, this indeed the cities having been laid waste, and houses being sold, and whatever by the laws of war is done by enemies, in this way has been written of the prophecy: 'The vision which saw Isaiah son of Amoz, concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.' And the times of the kings are usefully noted, so that God appears appropriately to each person's manner the things speaking in the prophet. 'Hear, O heaven, and shine, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: I have begotten sons and raised them up, but they themselves have rejected me.' 'The ox knows him who has acquired, and the donkey the manger of his master; but Israel did not know me, and the people did not understand.' What is the matter, who is the word, and what would it be necessary to examine/scrutinize to make manifest? For the blessed prophet testifies just as both heaven and earth, and in doing this he does not deny God, but rather, he says that the words are not his own, but rather of God.

That altogether and in every way toward an end they shall emerge through this, signaling, and with the terrors of suffering subduing those who listen. For it is impossible to deceive God; at the same time also that, just as I am, preparing. pass_b_english: Logos 1. The vision which Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw, which he saw concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judah. No one would dare to lie about what was said concerning the holy prophets, claiming that they did not receive knowledge of the things to come through the shining of the Holy Spirit upon them, resounding in the mind; rather, it is also true of them that, when they spoke of these things, they were beholders of them.

It seems, therefore, that the blessed prophet Isaiah, through the eyes of the intellect, beheld the sufferings that are to come concerning Judah. He saw the phalanxes of the enemies trampling the earth, the cities being laid waste, houses being sold, and all that is done by enemies according to the laws of war; in this way, these things have been written in the prophecy: 'The vision which Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw, concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.'
The times of the kings are usefully noted, so that God may appear to each person according to their own manner in the things spoken through the prophet.
Hear, O heaven, and shine, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: 'I have begotten and raised up sons, but they have rejected me' (Isaiah 1:2).

'The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger; but Israel did not know me, and my people did not understand' (Isaiah 1:3). What is the matter, what is the word, and what must be scrutinized to make it manifest?
For the blessed prophet testifies as both heaven and earth, and in doing so he does not deny God; rather, he asserts that the words are not his own, but are instead of God.
That altogether and in every way they shall emerge toward an end through this, serving as signs and subduing those who listen with the terrors of suffering.
For it is impossible to deceive God; and at the same time, just as I am, He is preparing.

Because it was destined that the proclamations against Judea and Jerusalem be made, and that He should forewarn of sufferings beyond all words and of unendurable misfortunes, He did not fail to know that altogether and in every way, those for whom the Word is, shall be unheeded by the judgments.
Therefore, He says, 'Lord, to speak such things to them,' having most skillfully divided the mind of the impious, as if stripping away the unjust judgments.

For if a mediator and servant were received, and [one] perverting the words from above and from God, how could anyone justly be angry at him? Rather, how could he not be angry according to God of the one who has spoken the things out of wrath...
